facts.label: Perdi o celular
facts.sub: Diga o que perdeu, onde viu pela última vez e como ele é. Cor e capa ajudam muito a achar o aparelho.

facts.label: Achados e perdidos
facts.sub: Em muitas estações de trem e metrô dos EUA há um balcão de achados e perdidos. Muitas empresas também têm formulário online. Vá logo, porque os objetos costumam ficar guardados só por um tempo limitado.

facts.label: Leve documento
facts.sub: Para pegar o celular, o atendente costuma pedir que você descreva o aparelho e mostre um documento com foto. Isso protege o dono. Se não puder ir, pergunte se outra pessoa pode buscar com uma autorização.

compare.br: In Brazil, many people say “perdi o celular” and call their own number or ask people at the station.
compare.us: In the USA, people often go to the lost and found office or use a website form at the transit company.
compare.tip: Say: “I lost my phone on the train. It’s black, with a blue case.”
compare.ask: How do you describe your phone in English?

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Many train and bus systems have a lost and found office.
items.why: You can often call, visit, or fill out a form online.

items.s: The staff can give your phone to anyone who asks.
items.why: They usually ask you to describe it and show who you are.

items.s: A good answer to “What does it look like?” gives color and case.
items.why: Short details like “black, with a blue case” help a lot.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

pages.title: Where is my phone? · 1/3
paragraphs: Dee is in **Chicago**. She gets off the train at a big station. She puts her hand in her pocket, but it is empty. “**Oh no, I lost my phone!**” she says.
Dee goes to the help desk. A worker, Evan, is there. “**Where did you last see it?**” he asks. “**On the train, I think.**” “**What does it look like?**” “**It’s black, with a blue case.**”

pages.title: Where is my phone? · 2/3
paragraphs: “**Let me call the lost and found**,” Evan says. He dials a number. “**Hello, did someone find a phone? It’s black, with a blue case.**” He waits. Dee looks at the clock. She feels worried.
Then Evan smiles. “**Good news. They have it.**” “**Thank goodness!**” Dee says. “**Thank you so much.**” The phone is at the station on the next line. She can pick it up before five o’clock.

pages.title: Where is my phone? · 3/3
paragraphs: Dee borrows Evan’s phone for a minute and sends a message to her friend: “I lost my phone, but I found it.” She wants to keep in touch with her friends. She thinks about “The Golden Girls,” a TV comedy about four friends. They talk a lot, and they always **keep an eye on** each other. Dee smiles and goes to get her phone.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: A letra ph em phone soa como f, não como p. Brasileiros costumam acertar, mas às vezes dizem “fone” com o o fechado. O som certo é um ditongo: foun.
pages.how: Encoste os dentes de cima no lábio de baixo e solte o ar, sem vibrar a garganta. Depois feche a boca em um o arredondado que termina em u: “foun”. O n final é com a língua atrás dos dentes.
pages.tip: Treine “phone, photo, phrase” em sequência, sentindo os dentes no lábio.
